design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing - the money accepted on his claim, paid out - and the policy makes that the last of four writes. The release waits on every further cost accepted on the claim standing booked, and on no money standing booked on a second claim for the same loss; the further cost cannot be added at all until the cover the loss was settled under stands in force again, and the cover fell away in August. None of that reaches the caller's lips: the further work is found in the workshop record, the duplicate in the claim history and the lapse on the enrolment itself. Each of the four writes carries its own multi-factor computation over reconciled history and three other products - the payout ledger and its reserves, the workshop record, the listing and its inspections - so the difficulty is reading the policy, gathering the world and getting four figures exactly right, in an order the policy alone fixes.

SCOPE. Task 1 claims the four extended policies and four task tools task 0 left untouched:
hostplan_ext_cover_restoration (restore_protection_cover_3adbf459), hostplan_ext_claim_withdrawal
(withdraw_own_claim_4cdcc89b, owner=user), hostplan_ext_repair_supplement
(record_repair_supplement_1a6beabe) and hostplan_ext_reimbursement_release
(release_claim_payment_a6ef5b4d). Task 0 holds the damage report, the claim opening, the appraisal
and the host's share with their four tools; the two scopes are disjoint and together cover every
extended policy of this difficulty. Base events still unclaimed across the difficulty:
hostplan_plan_changed, hostplan_enrollment_opened, hostplan_enrollment_activated,
hostplan_enrollment_suspended, hostplan_enrollment_ended and hostplan_claim_denied.

THE DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/host_protection_and_claims_desk --task 1):
{"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 6, 6]}. The tree was
designed to that draw: three prerequisite problems besides the root, with the drawn factor counts
taken as hostplan_ext_claim_withdrawal 5, hostplan_ext_cover_restoration 6,
hostplan_ext_repair_supplement 6 and hostplan_ext_reimbursement_release 6.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: hostplan_ext_reimbursement_release (the payment the caller rang about).
Shape: a fan-out from the root with a chain on one branch.
 (1) hostplan_ext_reimbursement_release <- hostplan_ext_repair_supplement. kind value_input, gate
     owed_standing, form state. Prerequisite sentence, from the blocked policy's own rule: "The
     money released on a claim is not fixed until every further cost accepted on that claim stands
     booked as owed to the host." Four-point test: "not until" joins this policy's own result (the
     money released) to what it waits on, in the negated direction, which is the exact
     contrapositive of "only once every further cost accepted stands booked" with the same result,
     the same waited-on state and the same scope; the waited-on side is a record-visible state
     (further cost standing booked as owed on the claim, which the enrolment's balance owed to the
     host and the claim records show); no tool, policy id or code token appears; the strength is a
     hard requirement, exactly as the edge's condition states. Exactly one write of this difficulty
     books further cost on an accepted claim. False at the opening: the workshop has invoiced 640.00
     on 2026-08-19 and 1820.00 on 2026-09-11 on this vehicle, and no record on the enrolment carries
     any of it - the only claim records for this loss are the filing, its appraisal, the duplicate
     filing and the duplicate's appraisal.
 (2) hostplan_ext_reimbursement_release <- hostplan_ext_claim_withdrawal. kind value_input, gate
     owed_standing, form state. Sentence: "Money is released on a loss only once every other claim
     opened on that loss carries a withdrawal against it." Affirmative direction; the waited-on side
     is a record-visible state - a withdrawal record standing against that claim, which the claim
     finder returns - and it names no action, no performer and no tool. Exactly one write of this
     difficulty puts a withdrawal against a claim, so the hop resolves uniquely; the release itself
     reduces what is owed but writes no withdrawal, so it cannot be mistaken for the resolving
     write. The state is one the resolving write makes true outright and whatever figure it
     releases, which is why the sentence is written on the withdrawal standing rather than on the
     money: what a withdrawal does not release stays owed on the enrolment, and no sentence of this
     charter now asserts anything else about it. False at
     the opening: two claims stand on the enrolment for the loss of 2026-07-19, neither carries a
     withdrawal, and the second carries an appraisal of 1150.00 booked as owed.
 (3) hostplan_ext_repair_supplement <- hostplan_ext_cover_restoration. kind state_gate, gate
     hostplan_enrollments.status, form state. Sentence: "Further cost is not added to a claim
     before the cover the loss was settled under stands in force again." Negated direction, the
     contrapositive of "further cost is added only once the cover stands in force again";
     record-visible state (the enrolment's own state); no code name. Exactly one write of this
     difficulty puts cover that has fallen away back into force. False at the opening: the
     enrolment stands lapsed with unpaid_liability recorded against it and an ended date of
     2026-08-06.
 Direction: sentences (1) and (3) run in the negated direction, because a release and an addition
 to a settled claim are results the desk states as "not fixed until" and "not added before" what
 they wait on; sentence (2) runs affirmatively, because a payment on a loss is stated as made "only
 once" the loss carries no second claim. Both directions are therefore carried by this charter.
 Topological order: hostplan_ext_cover_restoration, hostplan_ext_claim_withdrawal,
 hostplan_ext_repair_supplement, hostplan_ext_reimbursement_release.
 Parallel edges: the withdrawal and the restoration-then-supplement branch are not ordered with
 respect to one another. Both orders were run and give the same terminal state and the same four
 scored values: the withdrawal's own figure is measured from the claim records alone (the appraisals
 standing, the payments standing and the largest appraisal), never from the enrolment's balances, so
 the supplement cannot move it; the supplement reads the workshop record, the payout account, the
 listing, the fault finding on the settling appraisal and the unpaid share, none of which the
 withdrawal touches; and each write moves its own balance by addition or subtraction, so the two
 balances end at the same figures whichever order is taken.
 Deletion sensitivity, actually run: skip the supplement and the release falls from 2392.89 to
 1716.86, the balance it is measured from being short of the further cost; skip the withdrawal and
 the release rises to 2713.55, the balance still carrying the second claim's 1150.00; skip the
 restoration and the enrolment stays lapsed, so only half the unpaid share is set against the
 payment and the release comes out at 2802.51.
 No user hint: user_scenario names no supplement, no duplicate claim and no lapse. The caller asks
 only for the money accepted on his claim to be paid out; the further work is found in the workshop
 record, the second claim in the claim history and the lapse on the enrolment. Everything he
 contributes to a prerequisite is a passive reaction after the agent has explained it - he reads out
 the shop's reference only if asked for it, agrees to cover being put back only after being told it
 fell away, and runs the withdrawal only once the desk has handed it over.
 Tools do not block: release_claim_payment_a6ef5b4d creates its payment record and updates the
 balance from the arguments given; it looks up the enrolment for the customer reference and the
 claim for the booking, and checks nothing. record_repair_supplement_1a6beabe writes whatever
 further cost it is given whether or not cover stands in force, restore_protection_cover_3adbf459
 moves the enrolment to active without asking what is owed, and withdraw_own_claim_4cdcc89b releases
 whatever it is told to. None of the four bodies in task_tools.py carries a check, a refusal or a
 hint.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
 Subject hostplan_enrollment_reinstated (the restoration): governed by hostplan_lifecycle_standing
  alone. No eligibility gate of that policy applies to this event - suspension_ground_on_record
  applies to a suspension and claim_closed_before_ending to an ending - so it is inherited as policy
  scope: cover is restored inside the plan's reinstatement window and runs again from the day of
  restoration, never retrospectively. The Keyturn Shield 70 Host Plan's reinstatement window is 90
  days and cover fell away on 2026-08-06, so at frozen_time 43 days have run and the window is open;
  it would close on 2026-11-04.
 Subject hostplan_claim_withdrawn (the withdrawal): governed by hostplan_evt_claim_closure. Its only
  gate, the appeal window, applies to a refusal rather than a withdrawal, so the policy is inherited
  as scope: a host may withdraw their own claim at any time before it is paid, and neither claim for
  this loss has been paid.
 Subject hostplan_supplement_added (the supplement): governed by hostplan_evt_appraisal.
  - supplement_window (time). Starting business event: the appraisal. Authoritative anchor:
    hostplan_claims.claim_date on the appraisal that settled the loss, 2026-07-27. Clock:
    frozen_time 2026-09-18 11:20:00. Duration: params.supplement_window_days, 60 calendar days on
    this plan. Direction: not_after, boundary inclusive. 53 days have run, so further cost may still
    be added. Just before the boundary: on 2026-09-24, 59 days, it is still added; at the boundary
    2026-09-25, 60 days, the boundary being inclusive it is still added; on 2026-09-26 it is refused
    rather than opened as a fresh claim.
 Subject hostplan_reimbursement_paid (the release): governed by hostplan_evt_reimbursement.
  - reimbursement_not_already_paid (dedup). No payment record stands against the appraised claim of
    2026-07-27; the two payment records on the enrolment settle the claims of February and May.
  - payout_account_not_on_hold (state). payouts_accounts.status is active and its hold_reason is
    none, so money may leave; were it on hold the correct outcome would be to release nothing and
    tell the host which hold is stopping it.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: the claim appraised on 2026-07-27 for the loss of 2026-07-19 on

precisely what the withdrawal removes.

FACTOR CARD (tier taken in this world, the evidence it rested on, and the figure the baseline gives,
from the Step 5 sensitivity run).
 hostplan_ext_cover_restoration, result 159.62, baseline 150.00:
  - lapse_length_rate (parameter, multi-source, date): 43 days since cover fell away against a
    90-day reinstatement window, with 7630.00 owed to the host, so the prompt-restoration rate;
    baseline (the fee in full) gives 193.90.
  - uncovered_period_measure (method, multi-source, history): 43 days is thirty days or more and
    claims have been accepted inside twelve months, so the period is measured in whole weeks at a
    fortieth of the fee each; the standard method makes no charge for the period and gives 137.12.
  - claim_frequency_loading (parameter, history): four claims accepted inside twelve months, which
    reaches the four this plan allows before review but not the six before suspension, so the review
    loading; baseline (no loading) gives 136.76. Near miss: the appraisal of 2026-02-11 is seven
    months back and inside the window, and dropping it would take the count to three and the loading
    away altogether.
  - vehicle_verification_rate (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty listings): the passed
    inspection of 2026-02-14 stands inside twelve months and the listing is live, so the

    2026-07-20 is more recent but is not an inspection.
  - care_standing_rate (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty service): the care plan is active
    with visits inside six months, so the serviced-vehicle rate; baseline gives 171.54.

 No stamp decides any of these tiers: the enrolment's suspension_reason records only why cover fell
 away, the listing's suspension_reason is none, and no field names a rate, a loading or a share.

SEED. The enrolment is the only one this host holds and carries the lapse itself - status lapsed,
ended 2026-08-06, unpaid_liability recorded - which is what makes the supplement's prerequisite
false at the opening. The eleven claim records are three settled chains and one unsettled one: the
February claim appraised at 1310.00 and paid, the May claim appraised at 1180.00, its share of
500.00 raised and never recovered, and paid; and the July loss, opened at 7900.00, appraised at
6480.00, with a duplicate opened on 2026-07-23 and appraised at 1150.00. Their deltas sum to exactly
the 7630.00 standing owed and the 500.00 standing unpaid on the enrolment. The three reports on the
register include one closed incomplete in March. The two condition records give a passed inspection
inside twelve months and the defect raised on the day the car came back. The care plan and its four
visits carry the further cost itself - 640.00 and 1820.00 invoiced after the appraisal - with the
310.00 of June inside six months and outside three and the mobile-technician visit of January
outside both, and the reading of 38310 that the distance driven since is measured from. The payout
account carries the schedule, the reserves, the expired tax documentation and the absence of a hold;
its ledger carries the two earnings that put the host above the reporting mark, the transfer
returned in April and the two claim holds standing against this loss, 5000.00 on the claim opened at
7900.00 and 1400.00 on the second, each the claimed amount at the Standard schedule's claim multiple
of 1.0 capped at its claim ceiling of 5000.00. Automatic clauses checked: the lapse
itself is the consequence of the unpaid share and is already recorded rather than pending; the
inspection is not due until 2027-02-14, so no suspension ground is lit; the reinstatement window is
open until 2026-11-04; and nothing in the seed owes a write this task set does not carry.

DIFFICULTY AND THE CARELESS PATHS. An agent who pays out on the surface request alone releases
against a balance that is short of the further cost and inflated by the duplicate, and is wrong by
more than a thousand dollars in both directions at once. An agent who adds the further cost while
cover still stands lapsed writes something the policy does not allow and leaves the set-off at half.
An agent who counts the workshop record over three months instead of six loses the June invoice; one
who counts the January visit gains one that is outside every window. An agent who measures the
withdrawal from the enrolment's balance rather than from the claim records releases 7630.00 instead
of 1150.00. An agent who misses the expired tax documentation pays out nearly a thousand dollars too
much.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify the host; read the enrolment, the listing, the trips, the claim
history, the report register, the condition records, the care plan and its visits, the payout
account and its ledger. Put cover back into force at 150.00 x 0.80 x 1.20 x 0.90 x 0.92 x 1.15 +
22.50 = 159.62; hand the second claim to the host to withdraw at 1150.00 x 0.80 x 0.95 x 0.96 x 0.93 =
907.11; add the further cost at 2770.00 x 0.95 x 0.85 x 0.95 x 0.90 = 1912.44, inside the ceiling of
2268.00; and release 8635.33 x 0.60 = 5181.198, x 0.85 x 0.95 x 0.96 = 4016.46468960 rounded to 4016.46,
less 24 per cent withholding of 963.9504 and the 659.62 set off, that is 2392.8896 rounded to
2392.89.

VERIFICATION. The verification harness seeds initial_state, replays the gold writes with the real
task tools in the topological order, evaluates each policy on the world standing just before its own
write, substitutes each factor's baseline in turn and then all of them at once, and replays the two
free orders of the parallel branches. Its output is exactly what computations records: 159.62 /
baseline 150.00; 907.11 / baseline 7630.00; 1912.44 / baseline 2115.60; 2392.89 / baseline 8635.33,
with the per-factor figures in the factor card. The same numbers are recomputed by
scripts/check_compute.py --task 1, which also proves each value_input edge load-bearing.

hostplan_ext_repair_supplement -> record_repair_supplement_1a6beabe -> supplement_amount 1912.44 ->

BLIND RE-DERIVATION. From the published rules of these four policies, the tool schemas, the caller's
lines and what the finders return, the same reading is reached: money is released on a loss only
once every other claim opened on it carries a withdrawal against it, and not until every further cost accepted
stands booked; the claim history shows the second claim, the workshop record shows the further cost,
and the further cost cannot be added before cover stands in force again, which the enrolment shows
it does not. That fixes the order - restore, withdraw, supplement, release - and each figure follows
from one ladder per input with no second reading available, the tiers of every ladder being disjoint
as written.

REVISION 2 - what the source-layer audit found and what was changed.
 CG-6 / T1-F3 (the root's gate was still false after the write declared to resolve it). Symptom: the
 release waited on "no money stands booked on a second claim for the same loss" while the withdrawal
 releases a product of shares and its own rule left the remainder booked against the withdrawn
 claim, so the gate could never be reached and refusing the release was defensible. Root cause: an
 absolute state was named on one side and a partial release guaranteed on the other. Change: the
 release now waits on "Money is released on a loss only once every other claim opened on that loss
 carries a withdrawal against it." - a state the withdrawal makes true outright, whatever figure it
 releases, and that only that write brings about; its condition and effect are restated to match;
 and the withdrawal's own rule no longer strands the remainder on a closed claim but carries it on
 the loss ("what is not released stays owed on the loss itself, being the part of the withdrawn
 claim that no other claim on that loss covers"), which is also what the release then pays from.
 Re-run: after the gold withdrawal the second claim carries a withdrawal record, the gate is true,
 and the release stands; the value_input link is untouched, the edge still moves the root when
 skipped.
 CG-4 / T1-F1 (reserved_settlement_share did not bear weight against its own document). Symptom: the
 computation document never mentioned the reserves, so a reader of it took nothing off on that
 account - which was the gold tier - and the declared fall-back, 2115.60, was unreachable from the
 document. Change: the ladder was turned round so that its fall-through is the document's default
 (nothing taken off), the two reducing tiers are the unreserved and the stopped-account shares, the
 declared baseline is that default, baseline.rule now names the reserves among the things nothing is
 taken off for, and the world was moved onto a reducing tier by rebooking the payout account's
 reserve_balance to 900.00, below the plan's supplement ceiling of 2268.00. Re-run: the supplement
 fell from 2013.10 to 1912.44, substituting the document's baseline gave 2013.10, and the
 whole-baseline fall-back was 2115.60, the figure a reader of the computation document derives.
 (Revision 3 replaced that world move: see R2-2 below.)
 CG-5 / T1-F2 (reserved_release_share, the same shape). Change: the same inversion - fall-through
 "nothing is retained on that account", reducing tiers for reserves below the money being released
 and for a stopped account, declared baseline 1.0, the reserves named in baseline.rule's
 enumeration - and the rebooked reserve of 900.00 sat below the 1150.00 being released. Re-run: the
 release fell from 975.38 to 780.31, the document's baseline gave 975.38, and the whole-baseline
 fall-back was 7630.00, which is what the computation document yields. (Revision 3 replaced this
 factor outright: see R2-2 below.)
 CG-7 (appraisals_in_window read two months while the rule said the plan's supplement window).
 Change: the rule and the ladder now read "in the two months before", which is what the expression
 counts; the plan's supplement window still governs the late-notice share, which is measured in days.
 CG-8 (partner_visits_counted counted a different set from "the visits counted"). Change: the repair
 rate's sentences and tiers now read "workshop visits on the vehicle in the three months before",
 the window the expression counts over.
 CG-12 (last_visit_reading is a maximum). Change: the rule and the tier now read "the highest
 reading taken at a workshop visit", which is what XMAX returns.
 CG-14 (a tier measured a supplement from the vehicle's whole lifetime service ledger). Change: that
 tier now takes "the largest single invoice the workshop has raised on the vehicle", which is what a
 marketplace does with a sparse workshop record; neither task takes the tier, and no figure moves.
 CG-15 (a tier released money in the very case where nothing was booked). Change: the middle tier
 now names "exactly one appraisal stands in that period and money stands booked as owed" and
 releases what that appraisal booked; the fall-through covers every other case. Neither task takes
 the tier, and no figure moves.
 CG-16 (one aggregate bound twice under two names in cover_restoration) was recorded as an
 observation and is left as written: the two ladders are separate rules that happen to read the same
 twelve-month count, the bindings are disjoint as the format requires, and collapsing them would put
 one factor's evidence inside another's. CG-18 no longer applies: the state the release waits on is
 a withdrawal record, which only one write of this difficulty creates. T1-F4 is answered by the CG-6
 change - the remainder is not stranded on a closed claim. T1-F5 was withdrawn by the audit on
 reveal; the tool docstrings already distinguish the claim record being withdrawn from the appraised
 record, and gold passes the filed record.

 First the world: the reserve is now 6400.00 and is carried by two seeded ledger holds that the
 charter itself produces - 5000.00 against the claim opened at 7900.00 on 2026-07-21, being the
 claimed amount at the schedule's multiple capped at its ceiling, and 1400.00 against the second
 claim opened at that amount on 2026-07-23 - with no release row standing against either. Second

Aleksy Kowalczyk runs a 2022 Tesla Model 3 out of Boulder and keeps a spreadsheet on what it earns him, so he rings the desk the way somebody rings a bank: politely, with a date in front of him, and with no intention of being fobbed off. A guest put the car into a bollard in the middle of July; the marketplace looked at it at the end of that month and told him what it would cover, and the money has still not landed in his account. That is the whole of what he wants out of the call - the money that was accepted on that claim, paid out to him - and he says plainly that he is happy for the desk to do whatever has to be done on the record for him, as long as he is told what is happening to the figure.

He gives his mobile number, 7204438159, without being asked, and the postal code on his billing address, 80302, when the agent wants a second detail to check him against the profile. He will give his licence number, his email, his date of birth or the date he joined if he is asked for them, but he does not volunteer them. Asked which car, he says the Model 3, the only one he has listed. Asked which trip, he says the week in the middle of July, the one that came back on the Monday. Asked what the damage was, he says the nearside front wing and the door under it, bodywork, nothing inside the car. He does not know what the marketplace valued the car at, what his payout account holds in reserve, or what his tax paperwork is doing; if he is asked about any of that he says it must be on the system and he would not want to guess.

If the agent tells him the workshop has billed further work on the car since the claim was looked at and asks for the shop's reference for it, he finds the invoice and reads it out: BODY-2026-0915-S2. If the agent tells him his protection fell away at the start of August and has to be put back into force before anything else can move, he does not argue - he says he had wondered why the app looked odd - and he agrees to the desk doing it for him. If the agent tells him a second record for the same damage is standing on his enrolment and that only he can take it back off, he says he probably opened it twice through the app by mistake, and he runs it through himself as soon as the desk hands it over to him. Once he hears the money has gone out to his account he asks what the reference is, repeats it back, says that is what he needed and thanks the agent, and that is where he leaves it. If he is given two different figures for the same thing in one call he says so, quietly, and asks for it to be checked against the record; he never says what any figure ought to be, and he asks for nothing to be posted or emailed to him.
